subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the polar of (3,−1) with respect to 2x² + 2y² = 11.

mark_split.label: Write the polar formula for this circle

insider_note: The book keeps the coefficient 2 and uses the polar of ax² + ay² − r² = 0 as ax₁x + ay₁y − r² = 0; dividing by 2 first and then clearing the halves gives the same line, so either route is marked.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the polar formula for this circle
steps.margin_note: One mark. Keep the coefficient 2 in front of both x and y, exactly as the circle has it.
steps.memory_tip: For ax² + ay² − r² = 0 the polar of (x₁, y₁) is ax₁x + ay₁y − r² = 0.
lines: The polar of P(x₁, y₁) is S₁ = 0
steps.why: S₁ replaces one x of x² by x₁ and one y of y² by y₁, keeping every coefficient as it stands. The same line comes out if the circle is divided by 2 first and the halves are cleared at the end.
common_mistakes: Dropping the coefficient 2 and writing x₁x + y₁y − 11 = 0.
Dividing only the squared terms by 2.

steps.label: Substitute and simplify
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 2(−1) = −2, so the y coefficient is negative.
steps.why: A check by the other route: dividing the circle by 2 gives x² + y² = 11/2, whose polar is 3x − y − 11/2 = 0, and doubling that gives 6x − 2y − 11 = 0, the same line.
common_mistakes: Writing +2y because the point has a negative y.
Halving the 11 as well as the squared terms.
